Groups of one kind or another, play a tremendous part in shaping our attitudes, thoughts and behaviors.

Think about this  if an individual commits a serious crime, punishment means removal from society by incarceration.� If misbehavior continues, the ultimate form of punishment it solitary confinement.� Depriving people of contact with other human beings through isolation or shunning is considered one of the ultimate types of reprimand.�

Social motives are very important in controlling individual behavior.� There is no limit to what people will do for social approval including killing someone, enduring humiliation, pain or death.� Many highly valued activities are undertaken as steps in getting other people to notice, appreciate, help, love or honor us. �Socialization is the process where people learn to live in harmony with themselves, other and their culture.� The family is the first and most important group involved in this process.� The most essential aspect of socialization is the development of conscience  the ability to distinguish between right and wrong. Along with conscience, family teaches its members about concern for others and respecting peoples rights.�

PEERS
A peer is a person of the same rank or standing and is often the same age.� A peer is an equal.�

We usually�compare�ourselves to others that are similar to us in beliefs and values.� These persons are said to be out reference group.� For example, your reference group may be your classmates or teammates.� Sometimes our reference group is one in which belong, other times it s a group we wish we belonged to.� We are attracted to people who are reflections of ourselves or who represent what we would like to be.


Peer groups assist individuals in obtaining personal evaluation that is objective without family biases.� Within the peer group, the individual is�compared to friends of equal ability, not to brothers and sisters.� The individual can feel secure in discussing a variety of sensitive topics and discover friends may have similar feelings and thus fell less awkward about their own feelings.

Identifying with a group allows a person to share whatever prestige and power the group possesses.� Some persons are so lacking in self confidence that even the slightest approval or disapproval from others will get them to act in a particular way.� The group has tremendous influence.
